title: LACKO AND OTHERS v. SLOVAKIA
summary:
In Lacko and Others v. Slovakia, the applicants—Mr. Ján Lacko, Ms. Júlia Demeterová, and Mr. Miroslav Lacko—are Slovak nationals of Romani origin, represented by the European Roma Rights Center. Their case focused on the vulnerability of Roma and Travellers facing repeated displacement and exclusion from housing due to discriminatory actions by local authorities and non-Romani residents. Beginning in 1981, the applicants and other Romani families worked and lived in an agricultural cooperative in Krásny Brod, but after its closure in 1989, they lost both employment and housing. Over the next several years, they were forced to move frequently, as local officials and residents in various municipalities—including Rokytovce and Ňagov—refused to allow them to settle, sometimes threatening violence or destroying their temporary dwellings.

The applicants challenged municipal resolutions that explicitly excluded Roma from settling in these villages, arguing violations of their rights under the European Convention on Human Rights, specifically Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination), Article 13 (right to an effective remedy), and Article 2 of Protocol No. 4 (freedom of movement). However, the European Court of Human Rights declared the application inadmissible, finding that the applicants had not demonstrated that the contested resolutions were actually enforced against them or that their rights had been directly violated.

This case highlights the persistent barriers Roma and Traveller communities face in accessing secure housing and equal treatment in Europe. Although the Court did not find a violation, the case reflects the historical context of systemic discrimination and exclusion experienced by Roma and Travellers in Slovakia and across the continent.
